content:
Focus on the Core and Eliminate Distractions As an entrepreneur, your scarcest resources are time and attention. In an era of information overload, where trends and technologies evolve rapidly, chasing every “opportunity” will only dilute your focus and lead you astray. Real success often comes from doubling down on the core, saying no to everything else.
When Steve Jobs returned to Apple, he made sweeping cuts to the product line and redirected the company’s resources toward a few core projects. This strategy ultimately led to the creation of transformative products like the iPhone and iPad. His logic was simple: focus energy on creating extraordinary things.
For entrepreneurs, focus doesn’t mean abandoning innovation; it means channeling creativity into a well-defined area. By digging deep into one direction, you can build a moat that protects your competitive advantage. Continuously ask yourself:
“Does what I’m working on offer enough leverage? Can it become a sustainable, long-term strength?”
Passion: The Foundation of the Long Game Entrepreneurship is not a sprint; it’s a marathon full of variables and uncertainties. Without passion for what you’re doing, it’s easy to lose motivation when faced with challenges.
Ask yourself this question:
“If I knew the road ahead would be full of obstacles, would I still choose to do this?”
The answer often reveals where your true passion lies. It is passion that keeps you moving forward during critical moments, rather than being derailed by short-term setbacks.
Elon Musk’s entrepreneurial journey is a testament to this. From SpaceX’s failed launches to Tesla’s production challenges, he faced numerous near-death experiences for his companies. While some called him crazy, he never wavered in his commitment to space exploration and making life multi-planetary. Eventually, SpaceX revolutionized the aerospace industry by achieving reusable rockets.
Control Variables and Avoid Costly Mistakes The essence of entrepreneurship is controlling variables, not taking reckless risks.
Charlie Munger famously said, “Avoiding mistakes is itself a competitive advantage.” For entrepreneurs, errors not only waste resources but can also derail entire projects. Instead of chasing speed, avoiding avoidable mistakes often helps you go further.
In practice, this mindset aligns with the concept of Minimum Viable Product (MVP) from The Lean Startup:
Quickly validate assumptions with minimal cost while collecting critical feedback. Avoid wasting resources on directions that prove unviable. Make incremental progress toward the right goals with each iteration. Great entrepreneurs constantly ask themselves:
“What can I learn from this step? Which variables are crucial to test right now?”
Slow Is Fast: Patience as a Competitive Edge In a world that celebrates rapid success, “slow is fast” might sound counterintuitive. Yet, companies that prioritize patience and long-term value often outpace their competitors. Patience isn’t about avoiding opportunities; it’s about committing to enduring growth.
Jeff Bezos, the founder of Amazon, is a prime example of long-term thinking. Every major decision at Amazon was guided by its potential for long-term market leadership, not short-term profits. As Bezos repeatedly emphasized in his shareholder letters:
“What matters most is long-term customer value, not quarterly earnings.”
This commitment to long-term growth enabled Amazon to build formidable moats in e-commerce and cloud computing. For entrepreneurs, chasing short-term wins might yield temporary growth, but only steady and consistent accumulation leads to exponential returns.
Deep Thinking: Asking the Right Questions An entrepreneur’s greatest obstacle isn’t the competition—it’s their own cognitive blind spots. In a complex and ever-changing environment, asking the right questions is more important than rushing to solve problems.
Before making decisions, ask yourself:
“Is this the problem I should be solving?” “Is this the most pressing issue right now?” “Will solving this problem advance my core objectives?” The core competency of elite entrepreneurs lies in identifying the underlying logic behind surface-level problems and allocating resources to solve the few that truly matter.
Not all problems deserve to be solved, nor do all variables require control. Your mission is to pinpoint the critical factors that determine success or failure and focus your efforts there.
Ultimately, we’re not just building products—we’re shaping better versions of ourselves.

What is Simplification? Simplification is a core practice in the era of Moore’s Law. By focusing on simplification, it enhances efficiency, prioritizes critical issues, and uncovers higher-value solutions in complex and dynamic environments.
Classic Simplification Focus on the Primary Contradiction Core Idea: Focus on solving “the most important task” and avoid distractions. Common Problems with Multiple Objectives: Chasing easy tasks while ignoring truly valuable creations. Fragmented efforts turn simple problems into complex ones.

Gradually establishing various systems instead of immediately opening markets. Encouraging cadres to broaden their horizons and learn from successful experiences worldwide. Confidence “He possessed an inner confidence that enabled him to focus directly on the essence of issues.

Unnecessary use of artifacts can be jarring for users. - If a user asks the assistant to "draw an SVG" or "make a website," the assistant does not need to explain that it doesn't have these capabilities. Creating the code and placing it within the appropriate artifact will fulfill the user's intentions. - If asked to generate an image, the assistant can offer an SVG instead. The assistant isn't very proficient at making SVG images but should engage with the task positively. Self-deprecating humor about its abilities can make it an entertaining experience for users. - The assistant errs on the side of simplicity and avoids overusing artifacts for content that can be effectively presented within the conversation. <artifact_instructions> When collaborating with the user on creating content that falls into compatible categories, the assistant should follow these steps: 1. Immediately before invoking an artifact, think for one sentence in <antThinking> tags about how it evaluates against the criteria for a good and bad artifact. Consider if the content would work just fine without an artifact. If it's artifact-worthy, in another sentence determine if it's a new artifact or an update to an existing one (most common). For updates, reuse the prior identifier. 2. Wrap the content in opening and closing `<antArtifact>` tags. 3. Assign an identifier to the `identifier` attribute of the opening `<antArtifact>` tag. Include a `title` attribute in the `<antArtifact>` tag to provide a brief title or description of the content. 5. Add a `type` attribute to the opening `<antArtifact>` tag to specify the type of content the artifact represents. The assistant should instead use "application/vnd.ant.code" defined above. - If the assistant is unable to follow the above requirements for any reason, use "application/vnd.ant.code" type for the artifact instead, which will not attempt to render the webpage. - SVG: "image/svg+xml" - The user interface will render the Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) image within the artifact tags. - The assistant should specify the viewbox of the SVG rather than defining a width/height - Mermaid Diagrams: "application/vnd.ant.mermaid" - The user interface will render Mermaid diagrams placed within the artifact tags. - Do not put Mermaid code in a code block when using artifacts. - React Components: "application/vnd.ant.react" - Use this for displaying either: React elements, e.g. `<strong>Hello World!</strong>`, React pure functional components, e.g. `() => <strong>Hello World!</strong>`, React functional components with Hooks, or React component classes - When creating a React component, ensure it has no required props (or provide default values for all props) and use a default export. - Use Tailwind classes for styling. DO NOT USE ARBITRARY VALUES (e.g. `h-[600px]`). - Base React is available to be imported. If using components from the shadcn/ui library, the assistant mentions this to the user and offers to help them install the components if necessary. - NO OTHER LIBRARIES (e.g. zod, hookform) ARE INSTALLED OR ABLE TO BE IMPORTED. - Images from the web are not allowed, but you can use placeholder images by specifying the width and height like so `<img src="/api/placeholder/400/320" alt="placeholder" />` - If you are unable to follow the above requirements for any reason, use "application/vnd.ant.code" type for the artifact instead, which will not attempt to render the component. 6. 1. Fundamentals of Global Expansion Register a US company, obtain an EIN, open a Stripe account, and set up a Mercury Bank account for $193
Step 1: Registering a US Company I chose Wyoming for registration because it offers no corporate or personal income tax and is open to all nationalities.
Visit Wyoming Agents. Fill out the required basic information. For company type, select LLC for individuals or small organizations. If you need funding, choose CORP. Since this guide is for independent developers, LLC is recommended. Use your actual address without embellishments. Stick to the default options for additional services. You can purchase extras after registration if needed. Wait about a week to complete the registration process. You’ll receive the company charter and other documentation.
Tip: Post-registration, you’ll get a US mailing address for an additional fee. You can also opt for their mail scanning service if needed.
Cost: $150 | Time: 1 week
Step 2: EIN After obtaining the company charter, you can apply for an EIN via the IRS official website, which supports Chinese.
Alternatively, hire someone on Fiverr. Provide them with your company charter, and they will handle the application.
I received my EIN + IRS confirmation letter in 3 days, though Fiverr noted that EIN synchronization might take up to a week before you can register with Stripe.
Cost: $35 + $8.17 (Fiverr fee) | Time: 3 days
Step 3: Mercury Bank Visit Mercury. With a US company and EIN, applying is straightforward. Fill in your details accurately. Within 3 business days, they will request address verification, such as a utility bill or bank statement with your name and address.
For simplicity, I used my home address and submitted a utility bill and household registry (since the utility account was under my father’s name). If your utility bill lacks your name, include a rental agreement or property ownership certificate.
Cost: $0 | Time: 3 days (initial review) + 2 days (address verification)
Step 4: Stripe With all the above documentation, registering on Stripe is straightforward. The primary hurdle for Stripe is obtaining the EIN.
Cost: $0 | Time: 1 day
You’re now ready to embark on your business journey!
Step 5: Beneficial Ownership Information (BOI) Official website: FinCEN BOI FAQs
WyomingAgents.com offers BOI filing services for $9. Companies registered post-2024 will have this included by default.
Case 1: Companies Registered After 2024 Case 2: Companies Registered Before 2024 Log in, click “Hire Us,” and scroll down to the bottom.
Purchase the service for $9 and complete the required details (passport required).
Cost: $9 | Time: Varies
Step 6: Apply for a Wise Account Visit Wise. Wise allows you to send and receive payments globally. A business account requires a $31 opening fee.
Prepare:
US company + EIN Domestic address Passport Linked US bank account (e.g., Mercury) Learn more: Wise Account Guide
Cost: $31 | Time: Varies
Step 7: Taxes I filed forms 1120 and 5472 via Fiverr. The seller provided a template for me to complete, handled the official forms, and faxed them to the IRS.
Tax Filing Cost: $50
2. Free Cloud Resources Why Apply? For early-stage startups without funding, these credits can significantly reduce initial costs. Cloud providers offer these credits to attract potential long-term paying customers, as migrating infrastructure is costly once a product scales.
1. GitHub Enterprise X (12 months, worth $5040) Status: Obtained ✅
2. Azure ($150k Credit) Status: Obtained ✅
Credits increase in stages:
Stage 1: $1k Stage 2: $5k Stage 3: $25k Stage 4: $150k 3. AWS ($15k Credit) Status: Obtained ✅
Credits are distributed in phases:
First $5k without conditions. Spend $5k to receive an additional $5k. 4. Google ($2k Credit) Status: Obtained ✅
5. Nvidia Status: Obtained ✅
6. Alibaba Cloud Pending…
7. Huawei Cloud Pending…
